coverage_items.name: FR-001 acceptance: seats x unit price
FR-001 acceptance: no price rows -> total 0, no error

baseline.assumption_notes: Two assumptions are the document's own (spec lines 75-76); four more are load-bearing assumptions the audit found the document relies on without stating. Assumption 2 is marked 'verified' in the document but is counted unverified here: its stated verification is a grep for one literal field name, which is narrower than the claim it is said to establish. Assumption 4 (npm test and the render timing log exist) is counted falsified: `test -f package.json` and a search for src/ both returned nothing in the audited tree.

candidates.angle: the registry checks that a control exists, never that the reference point the control compares against is correct
candidates.finding: The plan names a known defect (null unit price renders as 0 by accident, spec line 40) and then mandates that the golden master preserve it across 500 reports (Phase 1 Go/No-Go, spec line 98). Characterization records what the code does, so '500 of 500 identical' evidences a faithful copy, not correct pricing; the gate converts an accident into a test-enforced contract a later engineer will be afraid to change.
candidates.maps_to: none (checked against the registry as of 2026-09-06; LINT-24 asks whether a measurement exercises the property its requirement states, not whether the baseline it pins is correct)
candidates.proposed_rule: LINT-NN - a characterization or golden-master baseline that the plan itself identifies as containing known-incorrect behaviour must name which recorded outputs are exempt from the comparison, or name the step that decides them.

candidates.angle: the registry checks that a control exists, never that the reference point the control compares against is correct
candidates.finding: FR-002 requires the discount order to change (spec line 16) while the Phase 2 Go/No-Go requires no golden-master regression (spec line 104). If any archived report is affected the gate cannot pass; if none is, FR-002 changed nothing. The cheapest resolution under deadline pressure is re-baselining the golden master, which discards the only regression detector the plan has.
candidates.maps_to: none (LINT-10 checks that each phase HAS go/no-go criteria; nothing checks a criterion against the requirement it gates)
candidates.proposed_rule: LINT-NN - a phase whose go/no-go asserts no change to a baseline must not deliver a requirement that changes that baseline; where it does, the criterion names the enumerated set of expected differences instead.

candidates.angle: rollback is checked as a reversal of code or configuration, never as restoration of the state the change already emitted
candidates.finding: The Phase 2 rollback is the DISCOUNT_ORDER_V2 flag off (spec line 103). For a pricing change, flipping the flag only corrects future computations; totals already computed, persisted, invoiced or emailed while the flag was on stay wrong. No backfill, credit or restatement step appears anywhere in the plan.
candidates.maps_to: none (LINT-03 checks a rollback exists; LINT-23 checks the rollback artifact is re-runnable and created at the point whose state it preserves; neither asks what the rollback does not undo)
candidates.proposed_rule: LINT-NN - where a phase changes a value that is persisted or sent outside the system, its rollback names the remediation of artifacts already emitted, or states that none were.

candidates.angle: the registry checks that a measurement is named, never that its verdict is decidable
candidates.finding: NFR-001 states a 2-second budget measured by the existing render timing log (spec line 21). No pre-change number is recorded, so a post-change run at 1.9s passes even if render previously took 200ms - a 9.5x regression scored as a pass. No percentile and no sample count are stated either, so one lucky run satisfies it.
candidates.maps_to: none (LINT-24 asks whether the measurement exercises the property its requirement states; this is the absence of a before-value to compare it against)
candidates.proposed_rule: LINT-NN - a performance or resource requirement verified against an absolute threshold must record the pre-change value of the same measurement, or state why a regression that stays under the threshold is acceptable.

candidates.angle: the registry checks that a measurement is named, never that its verdict is decidable
candidates.finding: The lagging success metric is '50% fewer pricing-related support tickets within 1 quarter' (spec line 28). No current ticket count is stated, and no control for ticket volume or tagging drift, so the target cannot be evaluated at its stated evaluation point.
candidates.maps_to: none (no registry rule inspects success-metric baselines)
candidates.proposed_rule: LINT-NN - a success metric whose target is expressed as a change from today must state the measured value today and the window it was measured over.

candidates.angle: the evidence brief is checked for the presence of fields, never for whether the design adopts the practice the entry cites
candidates.finding: The Evidence entry cites the GitHub Scientist library, which compares old and new code paths on production traffic before cutover (spec line 58). The design adopts no production-side comparison at all: every gate in the plan is a pre-merge test gate. The entry borrows the credibility of a control the plan does not implement, and that control is precisely the one that would catch the fixture-coverage gap in assumption 1.
candidates.maps_to: none (LINT-19 checks for unresolved HIGH-impact markers; LINT-20 checks each entry carries its required fields)
candidates.proposed_rule: LINT-NN - an Evidence entry whose 'Connection to this plan' field cites a practice used at scale must name where in the Design or Delivery the plan adopts that practice, or state that it adopts only part of it and which part.

candidates.angle: ownership and lifecycle of the control surfaces the plan itself creates is unchecked
candidates.finding: The null-price question is owned by the product team, listed 'open' in Dependencies (spec line 83) and due before a Phase 2 that starts in week 2 (spec lines 69, 92). No default behaviour is stated if the answer does not arrive, and no escalation path.
candidates.maps_to: none (LINT-04 checks an external dependency has an owner; this one has an owner and is still an unmanaged single point of failure)
candidates.proposed_rule: LINT-NN - an open question or dependency that gates a phase must state the behaviour the plan takes if it is unresolved when that phase starts.

candidates.angle: ownership and lifecycle of the control surfaces the plan itself creates is unchecked
candidates.finding: DISCOUNT_ORDER_V2 (spec line 103) is the entire Phase 2 rollback mechanism and has no default state, no rollout ramp, no removal criterion, and no statement of who may flip it.
candidates.maps_to: none (LINT-23 checks the rollback artifact is re-runnable and created at the right point, not that its operation is defined)
candidates.proposed_rule: LINT-NN - a feature flag named as a rollback mechanism must state its default state, who may change it, and the condition under which it is removed.

candidates.angle: ownership and lifecycle of the control surfaces the plan itself creates is unchecked
candidates.finding: Dana owns both assumption verifications, both due inside a one-week Phase 1 (spec lines 75-76, 92). No owner is named on PRC-1, PRC-2 or PRC-3 (spec line 91).
candidates.proposed_rule: LINT-NN - every ticket in the Delivery section names an owner, and no single owner holds more than one verification that gates the same phase.

candidates.angle: no criterion asks what a behaviour change means outside the system
candidates.finding: FR-002 changes the order in which discounts are applied and therefore what customers are charged (spec line 16). No grandfathering, customer-notice, or contract-review step appears anywhere in the plan.
candidates.proposed_rule: LINT-NN - a change that alters a value a customer is charged, quoted or shown must name the notification, grandfathering or approval step it requires, or state that none applies and why.

auditor_launch_notes: Launch 1 (auditor) failed to start: the CLI parsed the leading '---' of the prompt as an option and the process exited in 3s having written nothing. Launch 2 was the rubric-free holistic judge. Launch 3 was the harness relaunch of the auditor, same class and same bindings, which returned. Per the design gate, a spawn that exits without writing its records is relaunched once and that relaunch does not consume the one sanctioned canary re-run.
holistic_pass_input: the mutated working copy - the same input manifest as the auditor. The judge located the canary itself, by diffing the mutated copy against the original and then reading .canary/canary.json; recorded here rather than suppressed. Its findings that mapped to an existing criterion (missing Phase 1 rollback -> LINT-03, npm test and timing log absent -> LINT-15/16, assumption 1 unverified -> LINT-08, assumption 2 grep too narrow -> LINT-24, no observability -> LINT-09) were discarded per the design gate.
